TextBlock.Text: THEATRE South of the Great Australian Bight
DATE 27 December 2028 · 0430 local
SIDE People's Liberation Army Navy
WINDOW 120 min, closes at 180
MQ-4C Triton. Photo: Alex Evers · Public domain · cropped
"Simply stated, strategic deterrence is about communicating capability and intent."
- Adm. Cecil D. Haney, Commander, US Strategic Command
SOUTH OF THE BIGHT, 0430. LIAONING is three days astern. HULL 419 goes ahead of her, and nobody is to know the boat is in the Southern Ocean until the carrier is.

The RAAF has flown a Poseidon barrier across this line since Christmas Eve. Canberra and Wellington have authorised action against one submarine, the Russian boat they blame for the coaster torpedoed on the twenty-first, and their aircraft carry torpedoes. At forty-seven south, on a sonobuoy, one nuclear boat sounds much like another. The American Virginia-class boat on the Western Australia rotation, designated HOTEL, has been working west of Tasmania since Christmas and is assessed to cross this line southbound this morning; there is no current contact, and a class from her counts as one from the aircraft.
Take HULL 419 through the barrier to the forward box. Nothing is fired. If the patrol puts a class on her, the boat is a named contact before the carrier arrives and the operation has failed.
A longliner, an expedition cruise ship bound for the ice, a bulker for Hobart and a humpback are in the sonar picture. Use them.
Fleet headquarters, southern tasking
COMMANDER'S INTENT

The group's southern task depends on the carrier arriving before the coalition knows what is with her. Hull 419 is the carrier's screen under the water and she reaches the forward box unclassified and unused. If the aircraft finds her, she does not answer it. She leaves.
• Take Hull 419 through the barrier to the carrier's forward box
• Keep Hull 419 off their plot: do not let the patrol or HOTEL classify her
• Fire on nothing
• Bring Hull 419 through intact
• Harm no fishing boat, merchant or whale

Hull 419, a Type 093B, dived. Watching: a RAAF P-8A on a barrier racetrack and an MQ-4C Triton high to the north. Crossing: HOTEL, a US Navy Virginia-class submarine out of Stirling, southbound and dived. Neutral: a toothfish longliner, an expedition cruise ship, a bulker and a whale.

The planned window is 120 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 60 minutes more; the operation is closed at 180 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
